items.title: Is Palantir's Lead Over Its Peers Already Priced In?
items.summary: Palantir Technologies (PLTR) grew revenue faster over the past twelve months than every company in its peer group, and only one company in that group earns a wider operating margin. Palantir also carries the group's highest earnings multiple. Over those same twelve months the stock returned less than the S&P 500. The operational lead is evident, but current market valuations appear to price in much of that outperformance.

items.title: Inside the Trump Administration‘s $215 Million Bet to Win the Quantum Arms Race
items.summary: The U.S. Energy Department launches Quantum Genesis Q, a competition to build an error-corrected, ‘scientifically relevant’ quantum computer.

items.title: Can Hewlett Packard Enterprise Stock Keep Running On Orders It Cannot Ship?
items.summary: Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) has returned 156% over the trailing twelve months, and the stock now sits right at the top of its 52-week range. The next leg is the hard one. What could power it is already on the company's books: orders it has taken and cannot yet ship.

items.title: This Doctor Runs a $2.3 Billion Health Startup. He Says This Is Why Walmart and IBM Couldn’t Crack Healthcare.
items.summary: Doctor-CEO Oliver Kharraz explained why healthcare keeps humbling corporate giants.

items.title: The Options Market Says Dell Stock Can Halve Or Double
items.summary: Dell Technologies (DELL) stock trades at about $588, and the options market has already priced where it is most likely to sit twelve months from now: there is a two-in-three chance it lands between roughly $290 and roughly $1,180. That band is what a holder is carrying, in dollars. It prices the size of the move and says nothing about the direction. The size is the part worth your attention.

items.title: What Needs To Be True To Buy Rigetti Stock Today?
items.summary: Rigetti Computing (RGTI) sells quantum computing systems into a market its own management calls early, which makes the buy question hard to answer. You cannot lean on earnings, because Rigetti loses money, which leaves its price-to-earnings ratio meaningless. You can measure what you pay for each dollar of sales. Here is that walk, one step at a time.

items.title: The Oracle Stock Question Wall Street Will Be Asking for Years
items.summary: Oracle's AI backlog is exploding while its stock has been cut nearly in half, and that contradiction is forcing a fundamental question about whether Wall Street has this completely backwards.

items.title: IBM Software Growth Slows: Will Recurring Revenue Support Recovery?
items.summary: IBM's Software growth slows in Q2, but recurring revenue, Red Hat and Data gains may help offset weakness in Transaction Processing.
